t.4.6.1: O Rāma, this Hanumān, my minister and the best of counselors, tells the reason for which you have come to this desolate forest.
t.4.6.2: While you were dwelling in the forest together with your brother Lakṣmaṇa, your wife Maithilī, the daughter of Janaka, was carried off by a Rākṣasa.
t.4.6.4: Before long you will be freed from the sorrow born of separation from your wife. I will bring her back, just as the lost Vedic revelation was recovered.
t.4.6.3: Separated from you and from the wise Lakṣmaṇa, weeping, she was carried off by him who had been seeking an opportunity, after he had slain the vulture Jaṭāyus.
t.4.6.5: Whether she dwells in the netherworld or in the vault of the sky, I shall bring back your wife and give her to you, O subduer of foes.
t.4.6.6: Know this word of mine to be true, O Rāghava. Abandon your grief, O mighty-armed one; I will bring back that beloved wife of yours to you.
t.4.6.7: But I know by inference that she was Maithilī, there is no doubt; I saw her being carried off by a rākṣasa of cruel deeds.
t.4.6.8: Crying out in a broken voice, "Rāma, Rāma!" and "Lakṣmaṇa!", she was writhing in Rāvaṇa's lap like the consort of a lord of serpents.
t.4.6.9: For, seeing me standing on the mountain slope, myself the fifth among my companions, she cast off her upper garment and her lovely ornaments.
t.4.6.10: Those things were taken up and kept safe by us, O Rāghava. I shall bring them; you should recognize them.
t.4.6.11: Then Rāma said to Sugrīva, who spoke pleasingly: "Bring it quickly, friend; why do you delay?"
t.4.6.12: Thus addressed, Sugrīva then swiftly entered a deep cave of the mountain, wishing to do what was dear to Rāghava.
t.4.6.13: Taking the upper garment and the beautiful ornaments, the monkey showed them to Rāma, saying, "Behold this."
t.4.6.14: Then, taking that garment and the beautiful ornaments, he became choked with tears, like the moon veiled by mist.
t.4.6.15: But he, overcome by tears that sprang from his love for Sītā, cried out "Ah, beloved!" weeping, and, abandoning all composure, fell to the ground.
t.4.6.16: Pressing that excellent ornament to his heart again and again, he sighed deeply, like an enraged serpent lying in its hole.
t.4.6.17: Rāma, his tears flowing in an unbroken stream, glanced at the dejected Saumitri at his side and began to lament.
t.4.6.18: Look, Lakṣmaṇa, at this upper garment and these ornaments from her body, cast down upon the ground by Vaidehī as she was being carried away.
t.4.6.19: Surely this ornament was dropped onto the grassy ground by Sītā as she was being carried away, for it appears just so.
t.4.6.21: Or where does that demon dwell, the giver of great calamity to me, on whose account I shall destroy all the rākṣasas?
t.4.6.20: Tell me, Sugrīva, toward what region did you see my beloved, dear to me as my very life, being carried off by that rākṣasa of fearsome form?
t.4.6.22: He who, carrying off Maithilī and enraging me greatly, has thrown open the door of death for the ending of his own life.
t.4.6.23: Tell me, O lord of the monkeys, of that enemy of mine, the night-roamer by whom she, my most beloved, was violently seized and carried off from the forest; this very day I shall surely lead him into the presence of Yama.
